title: Advancement Alignment Console
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: convention-honoring (probability 0.4)
Title: Advancement Alignment Console
Thesis: A unified command center surfacing operational and data gaps across NU advancement teams, routing each to alignment, integration, or KPI workstreams.
Why this frame: This is what a strong advancement-ops consultancy would build: a diagnostic-to-roadmap dashboard organized by the three named categories. Safe, defensible, immediately legible to a VP of Advancement preparing a campaign.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Dana Okoro
  Role: Vice President of Advancement, Northeastern University
  Context: Oversees annual giving, major gifts, and alumni relations - three teams on different data hygiene standards, different CRMs-of-record, and different fiscal-year cadences - 14 months ahead of a 2026 comprehensive campaign launch.
  Emotional state: Outwardly composed but privately anxious; she knows the silos are costing the campaign but lacks a single artifact to prove it to her cabinet and prioritize fixes.
  Pain points:
    - No single view of where a prospect record fragments as it moves between annual giving, major gifts, and alumni relations.
    - Quarterly leadership meetings devolve into anecdote-trading about handoff failures with no quantified severity.
    - Each team measures success on incompatible KPIs, so 'success' on one team masks friction it creates for another.
    - Technology debt (overlapping CRMs, manual exports, stale dedup rules) is invisible to the cabinet until it breaks at scale.
  JTBD: When I prepare my teams for the 2026 campaign, I want to see every cross-team friction point ranked by fixable impact, so I can sequence a defensible roadmap and brief my cabinet with confidence instead of anecdotes.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Director of Annual Giving: Owns mass-solicitation pipeline; consumes gap-detail screens to fix data-quality handoffs upstream of major gifts.
  - Major Gifts Officer Lead: Receives prospect handoffs; flags incomplete records and contributes friction reports that feed the gap engine.
  - Alumni Relations Director: Manages engagement data that should inform giving propensity but currently lives in a disconnected events platform.
  - Advancement Services / Data Operations Manager: Owns CRM hygiene and integration plumbing; primary actor on the Integration Health Map and adoption tracking.
  - University Cabinet (Provost, CFO, President): Audience for the readiness briefing; needs board-grade, jargon-light evidence the campaign foundation is sound.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Dana opens the console Monday morning to a gap scorecard ranking three months of cross-team friction into one prioritized list; she drills into the highest-friction handoff, sees the AI-attributed root cause and dollar-at-risk estimate, and assigns the recommended fix to a workstream with two clicks.

USE CASES (12) - the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Map cross-team data gaps
     Trigger: Dana lands on the scorecard and sees the 'Data Integrity' pillar flashing amber after the weekly sync ingests new CRM diffs.
     Flow: She clicks the Data pillar → the Gap Diagnostic Detail opens a Sankey of how a prospect record moves between teams → she filters to records that lost fields during handoff → she selects the worst offending field (employer/giving-capacity) → she views the AI root-cause annotation.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro clusters thousands of record-diff events into named gap patterns (e.g. 'capacity rating dropped on AG→MG handoff') and attributes each to a likely systemic cause.
     Outcome: Dana has a named, quantified data gap with a dollar-at-risk estimate she can route to the Integration workstream.
  2. Diagnose organizational misalignment
     Trigger: The 'Alignment' pillar shows a high friction score driven by overlapping prospect ownership disputes.
     Flow: Dana opens the alignment lens → sees a team-to-team friction matrix → clicks the hottest cell (AG↔MG) → reads the AI synthesis of process conflicts → reviews recommended ownership-rule changes.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro synthesizes meeting notes, handoff logs, and ownership conflicts into a structured misalignment narrative with proposed RACI adjustments.
     Outcome: A documented misalignment with a concrete org-process recommendation and an owner.
  3. Audit technology integration debt
     Trigger: Integration Health Map surfaces a stale sync between the events platform and the CRM-of-record.
     Flow: Dana opens the Integration Health Map → sees system nodes colored by sync freshness → hovers the red events↔CRM edge → reads last-successful-sync, error rate, and records affected → opens the recommended remediation.
     AI role: Embeddings + Gemini 3.1 Pro classify integration error logs into debt categories and estimate the engagement-signal loss caused by each broken link.
     Outcome: A prioritized integration backlog item scoped with affected-record counts and effort estimate.
  4. Define shared KPIs across teams
     Trigger: Dana notices the three teams report incompatible 'success' metrics ahead of campaign-goal setting.
     Flow: She opens the Shared KPI Builder → drags existing team KPIs onto a shared canvas → the AI flags conflicting definitions → she accepts a reconciled cross-team metric → publishes it to all three dashboards.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro detects definitional conflicts (e.g. 'engaged alumnus' vs 'qualified prospect') and proposes a single reconciled definition with rollup logic.
     Outcome: A published, conflict-free shared KPI that every team measures identically.
  5. Generate 2026 strategic roadmap
     Trigger: After triaging gaps, Dana wants a sequenced plan to present to her directors.
     Flow: She clicks 'Generate Roadmap' on the Three-Pillar Roadmap Board → AI sequences open recommendations by impact-vs-effort → she reorders two items → locks the roadmap → assigns phase owners.
     AI role: Recommendation prioritization engine (Gemini 3.1 Pro) scores each gap on dollar-at-risk, effort, and dependency, then proposes a phased sequence.
     Outcome: A three-phase, owner-assigned 2026 readiness roadmap exportable to the cabinet.
  6. Track recommendation adoption
     Trigger: Two weeks after roadmap lock, Dana checks whether assigned fixes are progressing.
     Flow: She opens the Recommendation Tracker → sees status chips (Proposed/Accepted/In-Progress/Resolved) → filters to overdue items → nudges an owner → watches the scorecard friction score tick down as items resolve.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro summarizes status-change activity and predicts which recommendations are at risk of stalling based on velocity.
     Outcome: Live adoption telemetry that closes the diagnostic-to-action loop.
  7. Benchmark against peer institutions
     Trigger: The cabinet asks how NU's readiness compares to peer R1 universities.
     Flow: Dana opens the benchmark panel → selects a peer cohort → views NU's gap scores against anonymized cohort medians → reads the AI synthesis of where NU lags or leads.
     AI role: Wiki RAG + Gemini 3.1 Pro synthesize public advancement benchmarks and CASE-style sector data into a contextual comparison narrative.
     Outcome: A defensible peer-relative readiness statement for the cabinet.
  8. Resolve a conflicting KPI definition
     Trigger: An alert fires when annual giving and major gifts publish contradictory 'retention rate' numbers.
     Flow: Dana opens the conflict alert → sees both definitions side-by-side → reviews the AI's reconciled proposal → comments → approves → both team dashboards auto-update.
     AI role: KPI conflict resolver (Gemini 3.1 Pro) parses both metric definitions, identifies the divergence point, and drafts a single canonical formula.
     Outcome: A resolved metric conflict with audit trail and synchronized dashboards.
  9. Run the weekly readiness sync
     Trigger: Every Monday 7am the console ingests fresh CRM, events, and handoff-log diffs.
     Flow: Automated ingest → gap engine recomputes pillar scores → Dana receives a digest email → she opens the console to the top three changed gaps → triages each.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro generates a plain-language 'what changed this week' digest highlighting score movements and new gaps.
     Outcome: A reliable weekly cadence that keeps the scorecard trustworthy and current.
  10. Brief the cabinet on readiness
     Trigger: Quarterly cabinet meeting approaches; Dana needs a board-grade artifact.
     Flow: She opens Cabinet Briefing Export → selects pillars and roadmap phases to include → AI drafts an executive narrative → she edits two sentences → exports a branded PDF/slide deck.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 drafts a jargon-light, persuasive executive narrative tuned for a non-specialist cabinet audience.
     Outcome: A polished, evidence-backed readiness briefing in minutes, not days.
  11. Forecast campaign-readiness trajectory
     Trigger: Dana wants to know if open gaps will be closed before the 2026 launch window.
     Flow: She opens the trajectory view → sees a projected friction-score curve under current velocity → toggles 'if we resolve P1 items' scenario → compares curves → flags the slip risk.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro extrapolates resolution velocity into a readiness-date forecast with confidence bands.
     Outcome: A forward-looking readiness ETA that drives staffing and sequencing decisions.
  12. Digest 2026 advancement trends
     Trigger: Dana wants sector context before finalizing the roadmap.
     Flow: She opens the trend digest → sees curated 2026 advancement themes (donor-advised funds, AI prospecting, engagement scoring) → clicks one → reads how it maps to NU's open gaps.
     AI role: Wiki RAG + Gemini 3.1 Pro retrieve and synthesize current advancement-sector trends and tie each to NU's specific gap inventory.
     Outcome: Trend-aware roadmap framing that future-proofs the campaign plan.

KEY SCREENS (9) - every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Alignment Scorecard Home - purpose: Give Dana a 5-second read on overall readiness across the three pillars and what changed this week.
     Primary element: Three large pillar gauges (Alignment, Integration, KPIs) with a composite readiness score and a 'top 3 changed gaps' rail.
     Motion character: Gauges animate from last week's value to this week's on load (count-up, 600ms ease-out); changed gaps slide in staggered.
  2. Gap Diagnostic Detail - purpose: Let Dana drill into a single gap to understand root cause, severity, and dollar-at-risk.
     Primary element: A prospect-flow Sankey showing field/record loss across team handoffs, with an AI root-cause annotation panel.
     Motion character: Sankey ribbons draw left-to-right on entry; hovering a ribbon thickens it and dims the rest.
  3. Three-Pillar Roadmap Board - purpose: Sequence open recommendations into a phased 2026 readiness plan.
     Primary element: A kanban-meets-timeline board with three phase columns and drag-to-reorder impact/effort chips.
     Motion character: Cards lift with a subtle shadow on drag; dropping snaps with a soft spring and recomputes the phase header metric.
  4. Shared KPI Builder - purpose: Reconcile divergent team metrics into single canonical KPIs.
     Primary element: A canvas where team KPIs drop in as nodes; conflicting definitions render a red merge-conflict badge with an AI-proposed resolution card.
     Motion character: Conflict badges pulse once on detection; accepting a resolution morphs two nodes into one with a merge animation.
  5. Integration Health Map - purpose: Show the live state of every system-to-system data link and where debt accumulates.
     Primary element: A force-directed node graph of systems (CRM, events platform, wealth-screen, email) with edges colored by sync freshness.
     Motion character: Healthy edges have a slow data-flow shimmer; broken edges flicker red and emit a subtle warning glow on hover.
  6. Recommendation Tracker - purpose: Track adoption status of every assigned fix and surface stalls.
     Primary element: A filterable table with status chips, owner avatars, and a per-item velocity sparkline.
     Motion character: Status chips transition color on update; resolved rows briefly highlight green then settle into a muted resolved state.
  7. Peer Benchmark Panel - purpose: Position NU's readiness against an anonymized peer cohort.
     Primary element: Diverging bar comparisons of NU vs cohort median per pillar, with an AI narrative beneath.
     Motion character: Bars grow from center baseline outward; NU bars draw last to draw the eye.
  8. Readiness Trajectory View - purpose: Project when current friction will resolve relative to the 2026 launch window.
     Primary element: A time-series chart with projected friction curve, confidence band, and a 2026 launch marker line.
     Motion character: Curve draws left-to-right; scenario toggle cross-fades between baseline and 'resolve P1' curves.
  9. Cabinet Briefing Export - purpose: Generate a board-grade readiness narrative and deck.
     Primary element: A live-editable executive document preview with section toggles and an export-to-PDF/slides button.
     Motion character: AI-generated paragraphs type in progressively; the export button shows a brief generating shimmer then a success check.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) - every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Gap pattern detection (headline aha)
     User action: Dana opens the console after a weekly ingest of CRM diffs, handoff logs, and integration errors.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Record-diff events, prospect-handoff logs, KPI definitions, integration error logs, meeting/process notes.
     Output: A ranked list of named gap patterns each with pillar tag, severity score, dollar-at-risk estimate, attributed root cause, and recommended workstream.
     User benefit: Three months of diffuse cross-team friction collapses into one prioritized, fixable list - the moment Dana stops trading anecdotes and starts acting.
  2. Recommendation prioritization engine
     User action: Dana clicks 'Generate Roadmap' to sequence open gaps.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Open gap inventory with dollar-at-risk, effort estimates, and dependency relationships.
     Output: A three-phase sequence scored on impact-vs-effort with dependency-aware ordering and suggested owners.
     User benefit: Dana gets a defensible 'why this order' she can justify to directors instead of guessing.
  3. KPI conflict resolver
     User action: Dana drops two team KPIs onto the Shared KPI Builder or opens a conflict alert.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Two or more team metric definitions, their formulas, and the source fields each draws from.
     Output: A diagnosis of the divergence point plus a single reconciled canonical formula with rollup logic.
     User benefit: Ends the 'whose number is right' standoff with a neutral, auditable resolution.
  4. Peer benchmark synthesis
     User action: Dana selects a peer cohort in the benchmark panel.
     Model: Wiki RAG
     Input: Public advancement-sector benchmarks, CASE-style reporting norms, and NU's pillar scores.
     Output: A contextual narrative stating where NU leads or lags the cohort median, with cited themes.
     User benefit: Gives the cabinet sector context so readiness scores feel grounded, not invented.
  5. Cabinet narrative generator
     User action: Dana opens Cabinet Briefing Export and selects sections to include.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Selected pillar scores, roadmap phases, resolved-recommendation counts, and peer benchmark.
     Output: A jargon-light, persuasive executive narrative tuned for non-specialist board readers.
     User benefit: Turns a multi-day deck-building chore into a five-minute, polished, on-message artifact.
  6. Weekly change digest
     User action: Automated on Monday ingest; Dana reads the digest email and console banner.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Week-over-week pillar score deltas, newly detected gaps, and resolved items.
     Output: A plain-language 'what changed and why it matters' summary highlighting the top three movements.
     User benefit: Keeps Dana oriented in 60 seconds without reverse-engineering the dashboard.
  7. Readiness trajectory forecast
     User action: Dana opens the trajectory view or toggles a scenario.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Historical resolution velocity, open-gap inventory, and the 2026 launch date.
     Output: A projected friction-score curve with confidence band and a readiness ETA per scenario.
     User benefit: Tells Dana whether the campaign foundation will be ready in time - and what changes if she accelerates P1.
  8. 2026 trend digest synthesizer
     User action: Dana opens the trend digest before finalizing the roadmap.
     Model: Wiki RAG
     Input: Current advancement-sector trend sources and NU's open-gap inventory.
     Output: Curated 2026 themes each mapped to specific NU gaps they affect.
     User benefit: Ensures the roadmap is future-proof against where the sector is heading, not just today's pain.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: data-dense institutional confidence with editorial restraint - generous whitespace around dense panels, a single accent (NU red) reserved strictly for alerts and CTAs, neutral charcoal-on-bone palette, tabular numerals, precise 8pt grid.
  Hero treatment: The Alignment Scorecard Home leads with three oversized but calm pillar gauges arranged in a horizontal triptych, each labeled Alignment / Integration / KPIs, sitting above a quiet 'what changed this week' rail. The composite readiness score anchors the top-left like a portfolio NAV - large, set in tabular numerals, with a subtle trajectory sparkline. Nothing decorative; every pixel earns its place, evoking a Bloomberg terminal restrained into university-cabinet decorum.
  Motion character: Purposeful and brief - gauges count up, Sankey ribbons draw to reveal flow, cards lift and snap with soft springs. Motion always conveys data state change, never decoration. Transitions stay under 800ms; nothing loops or idles except healthy integration edges which carry a near-imperceptible flow shimmer.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these - the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. A spare editorial illustration of three interlocking but slightly misaligned gears labeled Alignment, Integration, KPIs, charcoal line-art on bone with a single NU-red highlight, for the empty-state of the scorecard.
    2. An abstract Sankey-flow texture in muted greys with one red diverging strand, used as the Gap Diagnostic Detail header background.
    3. A clean isometric depiction of three campus advancement buildings connected by data conduits, some bright and some broken, for the Integration Health Map onboarding card.
    4. A calm, board-room-grade cover image of an upward readiness trajectory line breaking through a '2026' milestone marker, for the Cabinet Briefing Export title slide.

FEATURE ROADMAP (3 phases) - the prototype demonstrates Phase 1 in working code; later phases appear as roadmap surfaces inside the experience:
  1. Phase 1 (Weeks 1-3) - Foundations
     • Alignment Scorecard Home with three pillar gauges and composite readiness score
     • Weekly ingest pipeline for CRM diffs, handoff logs, and integration errors
     • Gap pattern detection engine producing a ranked, named gap list
     • Gap Diagnostic Detail with prospect-flow Sankey and AI root-cause annotation
     • Seed dataset of 28 gaps, 10 teams, and 16 handoff events
     Success: Dana can identify and open the top 3 friction gaps within 60 seconds of first login.
  2. Phase 2 (Month 2) - Intelligence
     • Recommendation prioritization engine and Three-Pillar Roadmap Board
     • Shared KPI Builder with conflict detection and AI reconciliation
     • Integration Health Map with live sync-freshness coloring
     • Recommendation Tracker with status chips and velocity sparklines
     • Weekly change digest email generation
     • KPI conflict resolver with audit trail
     Success: ≥70% of detected gaps have an assigned, owner-acknowledged recommendation within two weeks.
  3. Phase 3 (Quarter 2) - Scale & Executive Readiness
     • Peer Benchmark Panel powered by sector RAG synthesis
     • Readiness Trajectory View with scenario toggles and confidence bands
     • Cabinet Briefing Export with Claude-authored executive narrative
     • 2026 trend digest synthesizer mapped to open gaps
     • Multi-provider AI fallback (Gemini primary, Claude/RAG secondary) hardening
     • Adoption telemetry feedback loop closing scorecard with resolution data
     Success: Composite readiness score improves ≥15 points and cabinet briefing is generated in under 5 minutes.

NARRATIVE ARC (6 beats) - the multi-timeframe user journey the prototype must SUGGEST through copy, seed data, and roadmap surfaces:
  1. Minute 1
     User: Dana logs in Monday morning and sees three pillar gauges plus a 'top 3 changed gaps' rail.
     AI: The weekly ingest has already recomputed scores and the change digest summarizes what moved.
     Feeling: Relief - the chaos has a shape she can read in five seconds.
  2. Minute 5
     User: She drills into the highest-severity gap and sees the Sankey of where a prospect record loses its capacity rating.
     AI: Gap pattern detection attributes the loss to an unmapped export field and estimates $2.4M at risk.
     Feeling: Validation - the friction she sensed for months is now named, quantified, and undeniable.
  3. Day 1
     User: Dana assigns the top three fixes to workstream owners with two clicks each.
     AI: The prioritization engine pre-sequences them and suggests owners based on workstream.
     Feeling: Momentum - she's acting on evidence, not lobbying with anecdotes.
  4. Week 1
     User: She reconciles the conflicting 'engaged alumnus' definition in the KPI Builder and publishes it to all dashboards.
     AI: The conflict resolver diagnoses the divergence and drafts a canonical formula she edits lightly.
     Feeling: Control - a years-old reporting argument is settled neutrally and permanently.
  5. Month 1
     User: Dana checks the Recommendation Tracker; several P1 items have resolved and the Integration gauge has climbed.
     AI: Adoption telemetry feeds back into the scorecard and flags one stalling item before it slips.
     Feeling: Confidence - the diagnostic-to-action loop is visibly closing.
  6. Month 3+
     User: Ahead of the cabinet meeting she generates a benchmark-anchored readiness briefing and reviews the trajectory forecast.
     AI: Claude drafts the executive narrative; the forecast projects readiness comfortably before the 2026 launch.
     Feeling: Authority - she walks into the cabinet with board-grade evidence and a credible ETA.

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (10 beats) - the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Dana lands on the Alignment Scorecard Home after Monday's ingest.
     System: Three pillar gauges animate from last week's value to this week's; the Integration gauge settles into amber.
     Motion/feedback: Count-up gauge fill with ease-out; amber pillar emits one soft pulse to draw the eye. (600ms)
  2. She reads the 'top 3 changed gaps' rail and clicks the highest-severity card.
     System: The card lifts and expands; the view transitions to Gap Diagnostic Detail.
     Motion/feedback: Card scales up 4% then cross-fades into the detail screen. (350ms)
  3. Dana looks at the prospect-flow Sankey for the AG→MG handoff.
     System: Sankey ribbons draw left-to-right; the field-loss ribbon renders in alert red.
     Motion/feedback: Sequential ribbon-draw with the loss ribbon drawing last and brightest. (800ms)
  4. She hovers the red ribbon to inspect the lost field.
     System: The ribbon thickens, others dim, and a tooltip shows 'capacity rating lost on 1,840 records'.
     Motion/feedback: Hover thickening with sibling dimming to 30% opacity. (200ms)
  5. Dana opens the AI root-cause panel.
     System: Gap pattern detection streams in the attributed cause and a $2.4M dollar-at-risk figure.
     Motion/feedback: Text streams progressively; the dollar figure animates up from zero. (1200ms)
  6. She reviews the recommended workstream chip ('Technology Integration').
     System: The recommended fix card surfaces with impact/effort scores and a suggested owner.
     Motion/feedback: Fix card slides up from the panel base with a soft spring. (300ms)
  7. Dana clicks 'Assign' on the recommended fix.
     System: An owner picker appears pre-filled with the suggested Data Operations Manager.
     Motion/feedback: Picker fades in centered; suggested owner avatar is pre-highlighted. (250ms)
  8. She confirms the owner and assigns.
     System: The gap status flips to 'Accepted', a toast confirms routing to the Integration workstream.
     Motion/feedback: Status chip color transitions; toast slides in from bottom-right with a check. (400ms)
  9. Dana navigates back to the scorecard.
     System: The 'top 3 changed gaps' rail re-sorts as the assigned gap moves to a tracked state.
     Motion/feedback: Rail items reflow with a 250ms layout transition; assigned card gains a tracked badge. (250ms)
  10. She glances at the composite readiness score.
     System: A small projected-improvement indicator appears beside the score reflecting the new assignment.
     Motion/feedback: Ghosted '+forecast' delta fades in beside the composite gauge. (500ms)

motion_contract.encodes: Count-up from last week to this week communicates score movement direction and magnitude.
A single soft pulse flags the pillar crossing a friction threshold — drawing the eye to where attention is needed.
Left-to-right draw mirrors prospect-record flow direction; loss ribbon drawing last and brightest encodes severity priority.
A 4% lift then cross-fade sets a confident, deliberate tone for entering diagnostics — momentum without flourish.
Animating the estimate up from zero gives weight to the stakes and signals it is a computed (estimate) figure, not a static label.
Two nodes morphing into one visually encodes the act of reconciliation — divergence resolving to a single canonical metric.
Soft spring on drop confirms a valid sequencing decision and triggers the phase metric recompute.
Slow continuous flow shimmer is the only idle motion — encodes a live, healthy data link; its absence (red flicker) signals debt.
Paragraphs typing in convey live AI authorship and set an authoritative, deliberate board-grade tone.
Cross-fading baseline vs resolve-P1 curve encodes the scenario delta — making the cost of inaction legible.

tracked-badge: small #1D6E64 check + 'Tracked' after assignment
severity-tier: 'Critical sev 92' word + number, never a bare color
states_per_variant: hover (tooltip: last_update + velocity; or both prior KPI definitions side-by-side)
success (color transitions on update; resolved row flashes #1D6E64 then settles muted)

components.name: list-item
anatomy: velocity sparkline (#1D6E64 polyline 140x34, aria-hidden + text equivalent)
variants: tracker-row: status chip + owner avatar + velocity sparkline + last_update; overdue surfaced
kpi-row: name + conflict_state chip + current/target tabular values + unit
audit-row: machine-readable timestamp (mono) + actor + action + channel pill (auditable change trail)
handoff-row: prospect_id + from→to team + fields_lost + flagged indicator
integration-edge-row: source→target system + last_success + error_rate + health word

components.name: modal
anatomy: centered dialog card bg #FFFFFF radius 8px padding 18px maxw 320
role=dialog aria-modal aria-labelledby; focus trap; returns focus to trigger; Esc closes
variants: owner-picker: combobox of workstream owners, suggested Data Operations Manager pre-highlighted, keyboard-navigable
confirm-publish: 'Publish canonical KPI to all 3 dashboards?' + audit-note preview
audit-trail-drawer: side sheet (260w) of change-trail entries, machine-readable times
crash-recovery: 'Restore your in-progress roadmap and owner assignments?' Restore / Discard
account-context: 'You are in: Northeastern University console' disambiguation for multi-account users
states_per_variant: open (fades in centered 250ms, suggested owner pre-highlighted)
success (status flips, toast slides bottom-right with check 400ms)
dismissed (Esc / Cancel / click-away, focus returns to trigger)
focus-trapped (Tab cycles within, no escape to background)

critique.summary: Fixed a critical syntax error in `Screen_gap_detail` where the `App` component was accidentally injected into the middle of the `fmtDollar` function during merge. Added missing `React.` prefixes to all hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, `useMemo`) across all screens to comply with the global runtime contract.

issues.description: Syntax error in Screen_gap_detail where App component was injected into fmtDollar function.
issues.fix: Removed injected App component and fixed fmtDollar string concatenation.

issues.description: Hooks destructured from React instead of using global React object.
issues.fix: Added React. prefix to useState, useEffect, and useMemo.
